restrictions: Messages are exactly 135 bytes; each is one padded block M || 0x86 with zero capacity (520 fixed state bits). Complete fixed-zero-IV SHA3-256 sponge with suffix 0x06 and pad10*1, prefix rounds 0..4, 256-bit digest.

This package (v18) is rubenmarcus's v15 (91f1424d, itself winglock's v14 f1cedf6b with Th0rgal) with five accounting changes and nothing else; the computation and outputs are v15's (proof V). (1) P's T3 runs as counted programs: hv_step tabulates each half vector with all 127 keys of the 7 levels (96 counted primitives, replacing 2^7 + 7 x 2^11) and match_step decides AS <= nb - 1 (83 counted, replacing 2^9); keys, matches and decisions are v15's (r5-mitm-1 trials 1-2), so P's output and 7,251,935 matches are v15's.

v17 change (2): caps by v13's run-free rule with reference 2^40 primitives (v15's P charge rounded down): X_MAX = 2^20 work units (v15 2^23), S2CAP = 2^21 (v15 2^24), and a new true-cost budget for B', B_TRUE = 2^29 units. No R5 or R6 run comes near any of them (largest attempt 190,240 work units; stage-2 count 315; true B' cost 2^28.27 units), so every R5 and R6 run is a complete run of v17 with v15's output (Lemma 6c).

v17 change (3): B' at its true cost (proof V.5). WK charges 256 primitives per row event; at two sites, Aff.add's table update (512 per entry for a one-bit test plus, when the bit is set, a w-word XOR: true 7 + 4w) and Aff.copy (256 per entry, true 3 + 2w), the true cost is far lower. r5.py tallies the difference (WK.d); WK's counter, CCAP and B_BUDGET act as before, so B' is unchanged; B_TRUE bounds the true cost. Every B' run used in the claim was re-derived from its label with this code (WK costs reproduce the logs). v17 change (4): development repriced by the rule v14/v15 use (counted prices of the submitted programs): D15 at v17's T3 prices from v15's published itemization only, G2's and C's B' at their true cost. v18 change (5): E stage 1 as unrolled blocks of 256 steps (75,386 counted per block instead of 256 x 364; proof V.7), also for G2's and C's E spaces.

No advice: the algorithm runs every phase itself, and its time is the sum of caps, fixed counts and organizer-recomputed counts times counted prices or stated bounds (proof 2, 6, V): P 2^29.0537 units; B' 2^29 units (B_TRUE) plus one update; at most 2^13 connector attempts of at most X_MAX = 2^20 work units (2^29.4539); E: K = 96 spaces, setup at most 2^16 units, 2^16 unrolled blocks of 256 Gray steps at most 75,386 counted primitives each (v18 change (5), proof V.7; 2^28.3829), at most S2CAP = 2^21 stage-2 pairs per space (2^29.3970). Algorithm 2^31.4335.

Development (proof 0.1, V, H2): every target-specific run whose result fixed, or under its plan could have changed, a number the algorithm reads, at the counted prices of the submitted programs. G2 2^31.1003 and C 2^31.9977 (B' at true cost, E spaces at v18's E), D15 2^32.3521, D16 2^27 (bound). Total 2^33.8145, claimed 33.82; preprocessing 33.64. Sensitivities, not claimed: E at 364 per step 33.92; B' at v15's budget 34.14; G2/C B' at WK prices 34.40; D15 doubled 34.26; all undone 34.62. A1 uncharged as in v13-v15 (proof V.6; 40.98 if charged).

Premise P (inside H1; success only): P outputs the trail of proof 3 within M_CAP. P's native run certified it at its level of 64 blocks (W* = 127 <= 2 x 64 - 1, Lemma P: every leaf with AS(alpha2) <= 63 is found, every other leaf has w1 >= 128), with 7,251,935 matches; the organizer recomputes the structural counts, the output core's level (r5-count trial 10), seed-picked cores (r5-mitm-0, 1) and P's driver on a sub-problem with its cap. If P certified nothing it would output nothing; every cost bound holds either way.

Probability space: the algorithm's own coins (B' candidate coins, connector coins), fixed target, no advice. Success is measured end to end (proof 5): R6, our pre-registration (plan and code hashed before any run, 48 complete runs of v15, all reported; each is also a complete run of v17, Lemma 6c): 44 of 48 succeed, one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson bound 0.8193. R5, v14's pre-registration, consists of complete runs of v15 (Lemma 6): 46 of 48, bound 0.874. Claimed 0.40; each study alone supports it.

Executed evidence (not the claimed cost): R6 and R5 (proof 4.2, 4.7, Appendices D, E), with 7 R6 and 8 R5 collisions as certificates; r5-R-0..7 re-derive 16 seed-picked R5 successes per review; r5-bpfull runs a whole B' from its label and reports its true cost (v17); r5-count checks the counted stage 1 step by step against plain evaluation and its longest path, the T2 leaf, P's driver and cap, P's certifying level on the output core; (new in v16/v17) r5-mitm-1 (trials 1, 2) checks the counted half-vector step over both full half tables of the output core (118,096 steps, longest path 96, vectors, keys of all 7 levels and w2 equal to the plain tables at sampled steps) and the counted match step on every level-64 match of the output core in 4 seed-picked blocks (longest path 83, AS and decision equal to the plain evaluation); r5-trail-0..3 recount T1, T2 and the half vectors.

rubenmarcus's v15 (91f1424d) is the base: its T3 meet-in-the-middle, counted stage 1, D15 and R6 are theirs. Th0rgal (7deb1595, with Subflatus3 and rubenmarcus) introduced the zero-advice framing; winglock's v8, v13, v14 built the algorithm; Subflatus3 (9bccf245) the zero-block half-sum match. Memory: largest phase about 2^28 bytes (key words add 15 x 32 bytes per half-vector entry, at most 2 x 9^5 entries per core: under 60 MB); declared 30.

The nominal reference identifier does not assert an improvement over published work; no improvement on the method of Guo et al. is claimed beyond the byte-aligned adaptation, B', the counted programs and the accounting.

heuristics.statement: Averaged over all of the algorithm's own coins (B' candidate coins, connector coins), the probability p that v18's algorithm outputs a collision satisfies p >= 0.40. Premise R (run selection and coins): the SHA-256/SHAKE-256 coins of labels fixed before the runs act as fresh coins, and the 48 runs of each pre-registered study (R6, ours; R5, v14's) are an unselected sample of the algorithm's runs, so that their success indicators are independent Bernoulli(p) draws. Premise P: P outputs the trail of proof Section 3 within M_CAP.
heuristics.scope: Only the success probability. Each R6 and R5 run is a complete run of v18 with label-derived coins (proof Lemma 6c): v18 differs from v15 only in the stage-1 program (same words, Lemma 4; proof V.7), the programs that compute P's T3 (same keys, matches and decisions, r5-mitm-1 trials 1-2), in B''s true-cost tally (B' unchanged) and in the caps X_MAX = 2^20, S2CAP = 2^21 and B_TRUE = 2^29 units, which no R5 or R6 run reached (largest attempt 190,240 work units, stage-2 count 315, true B' cost 2^28.27 units; every R5/R6 B' run re-derived, proof V.5). Each R6 run is a complete run of v15 with label-derived coins (proof Lemma 6a: v14's B', connector and driver code, P's certified trail, E as fes with stage 2 and S2CAP; no cap that should not act acted), and each R5 run is one too (Lemma 6b: v15 computes v14's outputs). Premise P concerns success only: every cost term of P is a fixed count, an organizer-recomputed count or a cap. Output correctness and every cost cap hold without H1.
heuristics.extrapolation: R6: 44 of 48 runs succeed; under premise R the one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson bound is 0.8193, so by R6's pre-registered rule the claim 0.40 is supported. R5: 46 of 48, bound 0.8746. The studies are not pooled. Premise R: R6's plan, driver, analysis, launcher, enumerator and P program were hashed at 2026-10-08T00:19:33Z before any run and made read-only; every run is reported (proof 4.7, Appendix E: per-run ledger with result-file hashes); the plan's only outcome-dependent rule is whether to claim; every other run made for v15 is listed (proof 4.1). Premise P: P's native run certifies the trail by Lemma P; it agrees with v14's exhaustive T3 passes; the organizer re-runs the output core's certifying level, seed-picked cores and P's driver on a sub-problem. Organizer checks of R5 as in v14 (r5-R-0..7, r5-bpfull); 7 R6 and 8 R5 collisions are certificates.
heuristics.limitations: Label-seeded SHAKE-256 coins stand in for fresh words (premise R). R6's failures, run order and timing are logged by us; the organizer re-derives no R6 run (the experiment file's 64-KiB budget holds only R5's table), but 7 R6 collisions are certificates. R5's limitations are v14's. P's full-scale certification rests on our native run (296 CPU-s, reproducible from Appendix A); the organizer checks 3 of 467 cores per review at the certifying level.

heuristics.statement: The charged development - v14's G2 (2^31.1003 units) and C (2^31.9977 units) with their B' runs at true cost and their E spaces at v18's counted E (re-derived from their labels), v15's D15 at the counted prices of v18's T3 programs computed only from v15's published itemization (2^32.3521 units), and our D16 (2^27 units, bound) - contains every target-specific run whose result fixed, or under its plan could have changed, a number that v18's algorithm reads, and these prices are the ones the cost model requires. The caps X_MAX, S2CAP and B_TRUE come from v13's run-free rule. Every other run produced program text or fixed no number of v17 (A1: proof V.6).
heuristics.scope: Only the development (preprocessing) part of the time and preprocessing claims. The algorithm's own terms (2^31.4335) are caps, fixed counts and recomputed counts at counted prices or stated bounds, and do not depend on H2.
heuristics.extrapolation: Proof 0.1 lists every run (v15's list, plus D16 and the B' re-derivations of V.5, which fix no number). D15 at v17's prices is computed from v15's published D15 itemization only (V.3): v15's rounded charges taken rounded up, v15's stated match counts at their smallest rounding, and only the match and key prices changed; no D15 workload is reconstructed. G2's and C's B' runs were re-derived from their labels with the experiment file's code (outputs and WK costs equal the logs; C's logged total minus our re-derived sum is added at WK's price) and are priced at the true cost of V.5, which is at most WK's at every event. Proof 0.2 gives the origin of every number. A1 produced program text, not an input of the algorithm (V.6), as in every qualified package of this lineage.
heuristics.limitations: Repricing development at the submitted programs' prices is the rule v14 and v15 applied (v15 priced G2 and C at its counted E). Sensitivities: G2/C B' at WK prices 34.40; B' at v15's 2^32 budget 34.22; with D15 also doubled still below 35.76. A1 (v7's design study, 10,432 CPU-s) stays uncharged as in v13-v15; charging it gives 40.98. D15's largest item is an upper bound (the stopped run is charged complete).
